title: From Atom Shell to Electron: GitHub's Desktop Runtime (2013)
explainer: Electron began life inside GitHub as 'Atom Shell,' built so the company could ship its Atom text editor as a desktop application written in HTML, CSS, and JavaScript instead of a traditional native toolkit. GitHub open-sourced it (still as Atom Shell) alongside the Atom editor's 2014 public release, then renamed it Electron in 2015 as it grew into a general-purpose framework beyond just Atom, and the same approach now underlies apps like Visual Studio Code and Slack. The rename marked its shift from one editor's internal tool into a general-purpose framework for cross-platform desktop apps.

title: Node.js and the Event Loop Electron Runs On (2009)
explainer: Electron works by pairing Chromium's rendering engine with Node.js so web code can reach the file system and OS the way a native app would. Node.js itself was created by Ryan Dahl and first demonstrated at a JavaScript conference in 2009, built around a single-threaded, non-blocking event loop adapted from the browser's own JavaScript engine. That event-loop model is why Electron apps can stay responsive while still doing file I/O and other OS-level work in the background.
